clue.text: Bland stuff a pub's cooked — left with little hesitation

indicators.note: cooked means these letters are prepared afresh, worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of 'a pub', the 's standing for 'is' and linking to 'cooked'
um is the short noise a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at the bland grub a pub has cooked, with a slight hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes PABU from A PUB; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pabulum is insipid intellectual fare, or literally plain food: a synonym for bland stuff.

clue.text: Film article dropped by little woman ingesting fluff when cycling? All right

definitions.note: the Disney film is The Jungle Book; drop the article 'The' and the title remains

indicators.note: ingesting means the woman's name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Jo March is one of Alcott's Little Women

parts.note: to fluff a task is to bungle it
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about a film where a little woman swallows some fluff while out on her bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' moves the first letter of the fluff word to its end. The film's full title starts with 'The', so the definition fits only once that article is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's story collection was filmed by Disney under its full title with the article.

clue.text: Sort of poker 10 removed from drawing room?

indicators.note: removed from means those letters are taken out of the room word

parts.note: an artist's studio is a room for drawing
the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A query whether a card game has been banished from the drawing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing room' suggests a parlour; here it is an artist's studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is a type of poker game in which some cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Stone from a ring, replaced before the centre's fallen out

replaced means the letters of 'a ring' are put back in a different order
the middle letter of the word 'the' has dropped away, leaving its two ends

explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' makes GRANI from A RING; 'centre's fallen out' leaves TE from THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock, a kind of building stone.

clue.text: Reply rudely? It's in shrew's nature

explanation.surface: Talking back is simply what a shrewish woman does by temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction says: take a word for reply backwards. REWSNA is in 'shrew's nature', as 'It's in' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Retorting impertinently is the idiom meant, cheek in place of a civil response.

clue.text: Check if baseball team turned up

parts.note: the Mets are the New York baseball team

explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or stop it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Linesman having a little nap?

parts.note: a kip is a short sleep
-ling is a diminutive suffix, as in duckling

explanation.surface: A football official seems to be dozing during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests a football assistant referee; here it is a writer of verse lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling was a celebrated poet, so a man of lines in verse.

clue.text: Post that supports article probing loud and aggressive speech

indicators.note: probing means the article pokes into the speech word

parts.note: bluster is noisy, threatening talk
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A commentator props up a newspaper piece examining a ranting politician's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short pillars supporting a handrail.

clue.text: Something eaten by 26, at first reluctantly imitating another rodent

clue.text: A better man than I am, nudging cryptically about 1st April

definitions.text: A better man than I am

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the other letter
cryptically means the letters of nudging are scrambled in puzzle fashion
1st means the opening letter of April

explanation.surface: Someone modestly nudging a friend with a cryptic hint around April Fools' Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptically' rearranges NUDGING into GUNGDIN, which wraps A.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem ends with the line 'You're a better man than I am, Gunga Din!', a quotation definition.

clue.text: Wife initially trimmed plain bit of sister's outfit

indicators.note: initially trimmed means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: simple means plain

explanation.walkthrough: 'sister' is a nun, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimple is the cloth headdress framing a nun's face, part of her habit.

clue.text: A strange pursuit involved getting soaked more than is normal?

definitions.text: getting soaked more than is normal

indicators.note: involved means the letters of the three opening words are tangled up into a new order

explanation.surface: An odd hobby that leaves its fans drenched beyond the usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersaturating a solution means making it hold more dissolved substance than it normally can.

clue.text: Cooking fish in prison — one with new governor at its head

fry are young fish

indicators.note: at its head means only the first letter of governor is used

explanation.definitionFit: Stir-frying is a method of cooking by tossing food quickly in hot oil.

clue.text: Cocaine and heroin? Me? I'm a mythical creature

clue.text: Theme: books and some poetry by male

clue.text: One out of the 2 just starting baked potato

parts.note: aloo is the Indian word for potato

explanation.surface: A cook just beginning a baked potato.

explanation.definitionFit: Baloo the bear is a character from Kipling's jungle stories.

clue.text: Quick! Hot spicy food going cold — out of bed!

clue.text: Quickly read second novel

parts.note: Kim is a Kipling novel

explanation.surface: Reading fast through a second book.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim a text is to glance through it rapidly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Old PM touring a land, drunk on the road hither?
